questions.prompt: A has condition number 10⁶. Roughly what is the condition number of AᵀA?
questions.explanation: The singular values of AᵀA are the squares of A's, so κ(AᵀA) = κ(A)². That is why the normal equations lose about twice as many digits as QR.

questions.prompt: Which pair of properties characterises an orthogonal projection matrix P?
options: P is symmetric and P² = P
P is invertible and Pᵀ = P⁻¹
P is diagonal with entries 0 or 1
P is upper triangular and P² = I
questions.explanation: Projecting twice changes nothing (P² = P), and orthogonality of the error makes P symmetric. It is singular unless it projects onto the whole space.

questions.prompt: In Householder QR the column x = (5, 1e-9, 0) is about to be reflected. Why use α = −sign(x₀)·‖x‖?
options: It avoids computing x₀ − ‖x‖, which cancels catastrophically here
It is required for Q to be orthogonal
It halves the number of flops
questions.explanation: Here ‖x‖ ≈ 5, so x₀ − ‖x‖ subtracts two nearly equal numbers. With the opposite sign v₀ = x₀ + ‖x‖ is a sum, and no digits are lost. Both choices are orthogonal in exact arithmetic.

questions.prompt: You solve Rx = y for upper-triangular R. Which unknown can you compute first?
options: Any of them, in any order
The one with the largest diagonal entry
questions.explanation: The last row of an upper-triangular system has a single unknown. Back-substitution solves it first and works upwards.
